issues.description: Tab key path still runs the old Enter-accept code, defeating the whole point of the option
issues.detail: When the user disables 'use_enter_for_completions', the guard only fires when key != Tab. But the enclosing block in keyPressEvent handles Enter/Return/Tab together. The fall-through still treats Return as accept for any item that becomes valid below. Either skip the whole accept branch on Enter, or restructure so Tab is the only accept path. As written this looks like it works but the original Enter handler downstream still fires for some items.

issues.description: Bad taste: special case bolted on top of an existing branch instead of restructuring the key dispatch
issues.detail: The new block is a wart inside an already-overloaded keyPressEvent. The accept-on-Enter logic should be a predicate at the top of the handler: 'is this key an accept key right now?' If you compute that once based on config + key, the rest of the function stays unchanged and you avoid the awkward 'hide + replay the event' dance. Good taste eliminates the special case; this adds one.

issues.description: Calling get_conf on every keypress for a static user preference
issues.detail: get_conf with section lookup runs on every key event inside the completion popup. That is a config dictionary walk in the hot path of typing. Cache the value when the popup is shown, or subscribe to config changes. Not catastrophic, but lazy.

Write 'key != Qt.Key_Tab'. The 'not x == y' form is a style smell and a code reviewer's tell that the author wasn't thinking about the expression. Trivial fix, but it matches the surrounding code's voice better.

issues.description: No test coverage for the new branch
issues.detail: Completion widget key handling is exactly the kind of thing that regresses silently. A single test that toggles the pref off, sends Enter, and asserts no completion was accepted would prevent the next maintainer from undoing this by accident. Patch lands without it; it lands better with it.

issues.description: Replaying the event via textedit.keyPressEvent is fragile
issues.detail: Hiding the popup then forwarding the event to the underlying editor works, but it couples the popup to the editor's exact event semantics and skips any focus/proxy logic Qt might insert. Prefer event.ignore() and letting the normal Qt propagation deliver it, if the surrounding code supports that pattern.

review.summary: Small, scoped patch that solves a real user problem (#12728) and mostly does the right thing — adds a pref, wires it through the conf page, gates the Enter behavior. NEEDS-WORK. The core complaint is taste: the gate is dropped into the middle of an already-busy keyPressEvent as a special case rather than reshaping the dispatch into 'is this key an accept key?' The downstream Enter path is not obviously short-circuited, and get_conf is called on every keystroke. Add a test, fix 'not x == y' to '!=', and the patch lands.
